We propose that neural populations must stop generating beta oscillations before they can initiate specific preparatory and movement generating patterns that may occur closer to the MO threshold . Thus , the generation of beta oscillations favors a low-risk state in which neural populations will not accidentally create patterns that cause movement , and in exchange compromise their readiness for upcoming movements .

fact: The study analyzed beta oscillatory events in local field potential signals by filtering at 25–40 Hz and applying a threshold to identify sustained beta activity.
source_span: To determine when the beta oscillatory events occurred , the following procedure was applied . The local field potential ( LFP ) signal from one of the electrodes used in the neurofeedback task was selected , and filtered at 25–40 Hz with a fifth order Butterworth filter . The amplitude of the filtered signal was estimated with the Hilbert transform . Each day , a distribution of amplitude values was computed by aggregating all rewarded trials from that day . A threshold was set at the 60th percentile of the resultant distribution . Then , all timepoints surpassing the threshold were labeled with a 1 . All other points were labeled with a 0 . Then , the length of each block of uninterrupted '1s' was computed , and if the block was longer than 125 ms ( so the oscillatory episode lasted at least 3–4 cycles as described in Murthy and Fetz ( 1996a ) ; Sherman et al . , 2016 ) , the block remained as is . If the block was less than 125 ms , all points in the block were changed back to '0s' .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the key method used to identify beta oscillations, which is central to the study's analysis of neural activity.

fact: Movement onset time during the arm-reaching epoch was defined as the time when projected hand speed first rose above 20% of its peak value.
source_span: To compute movement onset time for the arm-reaching epoch in the NR task , we used a method inspired by Churchland and Shenoy ( 2007 ) . First , the x and y cursor velocity over the course of the reach ( t x 2 ) was projected onto a unit vector pointing from the center to peripheral target . The norm of the projected cursor velocities yielded a single time series of projected speed ( t x 1 ) . The index and value of maximum projected hand speed was computed and called ( i , M ) . Starting at i , we scanned backwards in time ( i-1 , i-2 , … ) until the value of the projected hand speed fell below 20% of the peak hand speed ( 0 . 2*M , see Figure 1f ) . This timepoint was called the movement onset time and was used because it allowed for comparisons across different reach targets , animals , and experimental setups without having to define absolute hand velocity cutoffs .

fact: Noise in gene expression is an unavoidable feature in isogenic cells but can be controlled by cell-cell communication in multicellular organisms like Anabaena to ensure correct developmental outcomes.
source_span: Noise , extensively studied in unicellular organisms [6–8] , has been shown to play a functional role in cellular decisions [9] and in the determination of developmental fates [10 , 11] . While noise may confer an advantage as an adaptive mechanism to changing environments [12] , it must be tightly controlled during the development of a multicellular organism , in order to avoid its amplification and thus erroneous irreversible cell fates [13 , 14] . Unlike unicellular organisms , multicellular organisms can use cell-cell communication in order to control noise in gene expression .
selection_reasoning: This background explains why studying gene expression fluctuations and their control is important for understanding development.

fact: The Kalman Filter updates internal estimates by combining prior knowledge and sensory feedback, accounting for their respective uncertainties.
source_span: The Kalman Filter [45] is such an adaptive procedure that takes into account the precision of the current internal estimate of the required mapping ( the “prior” as it were , at that specific point in time ) as well as the precision of the incoming information in the form of sensory feedback , which is used to update that estimate.

source_span: To describe the behaviour of the Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters across the target shapes , it is important to note that the perception of the shape is noisy and thus cannot singularly influence one filter only . That is , learning for one shape will also affect the filters of neighbouring shapes in a graded fashion.
selection_reasoning: This key assumption explains how generalization across shapes is modeled, which is a principal finding area.

fact: The uncertainty of feedback for each Kalman Filter increases as a function of the difference between the filter's associated shape and the current shape presented.
source_span: We modelled this by increasing the uncertainty of the feedback for any particular Kalman Filter as a function of the difference in shape-space between the corresponding shape for that filter ρ and the current shape with which the system is being presented ρt along the continuous axis ( Fig . 6C ) .

fact: Neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) affect an estimated 2.7 billion of the world's poorest people, causing significant physical debilitation, lowered economic productivity, and social ostracism.
source_span: Neglected tropical diseases ( NTDs ) are parasitic and bacterial diseases that affect an estimated 2 . 7 billion of the world's poorest people , causing significant physical debilitation , lowered economic productivity , and social ostracism for afflicted individuals [1] .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the global burden and importance of NTDs, motivating the study.

fact: Five NTDs with available preventive chemotherapy—lymphatic filariasis (LF), trachoma, schistosomiasis, onchocerciasis, and soil-transmitted helminths (STH)—have been targeted for control or elimination.
source_span: Five NTDs with available preventive chemotherapy: lymphatic filariasis ( LF ) , trachoma , schistosomiasis , onchocerciasis and the three soil-transmitted helminths ( STH ) ; have been targeted for control or elimination , but resource constraints in endemic countries have impeded progress toward these goals [2] .

source_span: Because NTDs tend to overlap in geographic areas , it is logical that an integrated approach to mapping NTDs might result in more efficient identification of populations needing treatment [9] .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides the rationale for developing an integrated mapping protocol.

source_span: For trachoma , an ophthalmic technician examined both eyes of children aged 1–9 years for clinical signs of active trachoma ( trachomatous inflammation follicular [TF] ) and of females aged ≥15 years for clinical signs of trichiasis ( trachomatous trichiasis [TT] ) using a binocular loupe and natural light according to the WHO Simplified Grading System [12] .

fact: The Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) methodology is an operational tool designed for Ministries of Health in NTD-endemic countries to determine if the threshold for launching disease-specific public health interventions has been reached.
source_span: We describe an integrated NTD mapping methodology ( Integrated Threshold Mapping ) that can be used as an operational tool by Ministries of Health in NTD-endemic countries to determine if the threshold needed to launch disease-specific public health intervenions has been reached .

source_span: The results of the cost data analysis Table 4 , indicate that using the ITM methodology resulted in a 31% overall cost savings in Mali ( $6 , 968 vs . $10 , 039 ) , and a 19% overall cost savings in Senegal ( $8 , 442 vs . $10 , 372 ) .

fact: The ITM methodology used resources more efficiently than the WHO methodology in travel, supplies, and team training in both Mali and Senegal.

selection_reasoning: This fact supports the practical advantages of the ITM method, important for public health implementation.

fact: In Mali, the ITM methodology identified more sub-districts needing mass drug administration (MDA) for schistosomiasis, including some for whole population treatment, compared to the WHO methodology which recommended MDA only for school-aged children.
source_span: The WHO methodology indicated a need for MDA for schistosomiasis treatment among only school-aged children in the entire area , while the ITM methodology indicated six sub-districts in need of MDA for schistosomiasis among school-aged children only , four sub-districts in need of MDA for schistosomiasis for the whole population and one sub-district which did not pass the threshold for treatment .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a key difference in public health recommendations between the two methods, central to the study's findings.

fact: Compared to the district-based WHO protocol, the ITM methodology targeted nearly 46,000 extra at-risk individuals for schistosomiasis treatment in Mali.
source_span: Compared to the district based WHO protocol , the ITM methodology targeted nearly 46 , 000 extra at-risk individuals for treatment .
selection_reasoning: This fact quantifies the increased reach of the ITM method, important for understanding its public health impact.

fact: The ITM methodology uses program-specific age groups as indicated by WHO, with minor adaptations for trachoma, to allow use of WHO thresholds and reduce the number of people undergoing multiple tests.
source_span: In our ITM mapping protocol , we insisted on using the program-specific age groups as indicated by WHO with the exception of some adaptation for trachoma . The advantage of using these established age groups was that the WHO thresholds were applicable and that few people had to undergo multiple tests and examinations; only in a limited number of cases were people asked to undergo more than one test or examination .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains a key design choice that supports the validity and efficiency of the ITM method.

fact: The ITM methodology uses convenience sampling in villages to improve field practicality and efficiency compared to house-to-house visits used in the WHO trachoma protocol.
source_span: In each village , we chose to use a convenience sample for reasons of field practicality . Asking people of different ages to come to a central location in each village facilitated data collection and was much more time-efficient than house-to-house visits , such as those used in the WHO trachoma protocol .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a key methodological adaptation that improves feasibility, relevant to the study's main question.

fact: The ITM and WHO methodologies resulted in the same public health recommendations in the field testing conducted in Mali and Senegal.

selection_reasoning: This fact supports the validity of the ITM method compared to the established WHO method, a principal finding.

fact: The ITM protocol maintains the WHO-recommended disease indicators and thresholds for lymphatic filariasis, schistosomiasis, and soil-transmitted helminths but uses a novel sampling frame for more practical field implementation.
source_span: The ITM protocol maintains the WHO-recommended disease indicators and thresholds for LF , schistosomiasis and STH , but we used a novel sampling frame for more practical field implementation .

fact: To improve representativeness for the trachomatous inflammation—follicular (TF) indicator, the study selected a predetermined number of children aged 1–5 and 6–9 to prevent biased prevalence estimates.
source_span: To improve the representativeness for the TF indicator , we selected a pre-determined number of children between the ages of 1–5 and 6–9 . This was intended to prevent biased estimates in case the 6–9 year age group made up the majority of children being graded for trachoma because prevalence rates are highest in 1–5 year olds .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a key sampling strategy designed to improve accuracy of disease prevalence estimates, relevant to the study's methods and findings.

fact: The study used women above the age of 15 years to measure trachomatous trichiasis (TT) prevalence, based on expert consultation and literature.
source_span: After consultation with trachoma experts , we decided to use women above the age of 15 yrs [22] .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies a key measurement decision for a disease indicator, important for understanding the study's approach.

fact: The ITM methodology links the sampling frame directly to the implementation unit for mass drug administration (MDA) for each neglected tropical disease to improve public health action feasibility.

fact: The study used the district as the primary implementation unit for soil-transmitted helminths (STH) because a village-centered approach is difficult for large-scale national program implementation and supervision.
source_span: Because a village-centered approach is difficult for implementation and supervision for a large-scale national program , we decided to use the district as the primary implementation unit for STH as it is recommended by WHO for LF and trachoma .

fact: Both the ITM and WHO methodologies concluded that no intervention was necessary for soil-transmitted helminths in the two countries studied, confirming the reliability of the ITM methodology.

fact: For schistosomiasis, the study recommends using the sub-district as the implementation unit for MDA to better target treatment and avoid overtreating or undertreating subpopulations.
source_span: In the case of schistosomiasis , a disease that is very focal in nature , and for which treatment medication is costly and in limited supply , we feel that it would be more appropriate to use the sub-district as implementation units to determine needs for treatment because a district-based approach may result in overtreating or undertreating subpopulations within the district [23] .

selection_reasoning: This fact demonstrates a key advantage of the integrated approach in improving disease mapping precision.

fact: Using the WHO protocol would have resulted in tens of thousands of people in highly endemic areas not receiving treatment and others not in need being treated, as observed in Senegal.

fact: The integrated approach was more efficient in cost, transport, time in the field, and use of human resources compared to the WHO methodologies.

source_span: The ITM methodology used one vehicle to transport the team , versus 3 used in the WHO methodologies , employed a 5-member team instead of a 7-member team , and took about half as much time to implement as the WHO methodologies .

fact: Cost savings from integrated mapping include reduced planning and logistic preparations, which is valuable for overburdened health staff.

fact: Mapping is often the first field activity of an integrated neglected tropical disease program, and integrated surveys help demonstrate the concept of integrating vertical programs at all levels of the Ministry of Health.

fact: Although the ITM methodology resulted in substantial cost savings compared to the WHO methodology, the cost depends on the number of sub-units in a district, which can increase sampling size for schistosomiasis.

This means , for example , that the sampling size for schistosomiasis could be much higher using the ITM methodology than using the WHO methodology .
selection_reasoning: This fact qualifies the cost-effectiveness claim and highlights a trade-off important for interpretation.

fact: A more targeted mass drug administration for schistosomiasis is important because praziquantel medication is limited in availability.

fact: Health workers are not always well-informed about where schistosomiasis is most prevalent, as indicated by results from both ITM and WHO methodologies.

fact: Proteochemometric models can accurately predict phenotypic resistance from genotypic data even for novel HIV mutants and mixtures.
source_span: We conclude that proteochemometric models are able to accurately predict the phenotypic resistance based on genotypic data even for novel mutants and mixtures.

fact: The HIV replication process is highly error prone, leading to frequent mutations that can cause resistance to antiretroviral therapy.

fact: Computational methods for predicting HIV drug resistance have become available over the last decade and can perform as well as phenotypic assays.

fact: Current computational models for predicting HIV drug resistance are trained separately for each drug and do not consider chemical similarity between drugs or similarity between amino acid mutations.

fact: Proteochemometric (PCM) modeling combines mutant data and drug chemical data to improve prediction of drug resistance in HIV by explicitly considering drug-target interactions.
source_span: Hence it is likely that also for established drugs , chemical similarity can improve models by explicitly taking the concept of drug – target interaction into account , which is then combined with mutational information of the drug target itself . selection_reasoning: This fact defines the key method used in the study and its rationale.

fact: Previous PCM models for HIV drug resistance were trained on relatively small datasets and focused on a larger chemical space but smaller mutant space, whereas the current study uses a much larger mutant dataset and a smaller chemical space.

selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the novelty and scale of the current study's dataset and modeling approach.

fact: The current study uses a dataset of 288,138 data points, which is about 60 times larger than the largest previously published HIV PCM model dataset.
source_span: Previous work focused on a total of 4 , 792 data points ... whereas here a total of 288 , 138 data points are used . Hence , we expect a more generally applicable model resulting from the current study .
selection_reasoning: This fact emphasizes the scale and expected improved generalizability of the new model.

source_span: In the current project it is our hypothesis that we can train a single PCM model for each of the following major HIV drug classes using the AVG data: Protease Inhibitors ( PIs ) , Nucleoside/Nucleotide Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors ( NRTIs ) and Non-Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors ( NNRTIs ) .

fact: The large dataset and PCM modeling approach allow prediction of drug activity on previously unseen HIV mutants, which is important for clinical treatment of patients with new genotypes.
